notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A spotless, orderly city-state: divided main roads, tall apartment blocks and lots of greenery.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Main roads have black-and-white curbs and double yellow lines along the outer edge.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street name signs are green with rounded corners and a distinctive white font.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Mostly black plates with white text in one block; rarely older white-and-yellow or red plates.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green direction signs with white text; expressways carry three-letter codes.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road signs always sit on a square white background, which is unusual.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Warnings painted in big letters on the road, like the famous hump-ahead message.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Mostly lime-green buses, plus white-and-purple operator variants.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bus stops are shielded by concrete bollards with black-and-yellow warning bands.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Traffic lights hang on a curved perforated metal sheet.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Rain trees are planted along main roads.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street names often match the neighbourhood, which speeds up region guessing.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Straight roads, industrial complexes, cranes and shipping containers.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green sign posts, winding roads and a resort feel on the southern resort island.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Rural forest coverage by a Generation 3 trekker, sometimes with a camouflage hat visible.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A tiny island with a path made entirely of red paving stones.
